title: Northbridge Dynamics — inference security & hosting intake
summary: Introductory security posture discovery for inference usage. Northbridge explained strict data residency and SOC2 scope, strong preference for customer-managed KMS and RBAC integration. Redwood AE/SE covered Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs, SSO/SAML/SCIM, audit logs, and retention policy options. Agreed to send docs, propose short pilot on Dedicated with KMS integration, and schedule a deeper SE-run architecture review.
topics: RBAC, audit logs, and log retention
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and costs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (CTO, Northbridge), Sara Patel (Head of Platform), Ethan Morales (Security Eng)

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Marcus our solutions engineer is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya Kaur: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to get into our security constraints for any inference platform, and like high level SOC2 scope and KMS.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Great — we'll cover Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and focus on the security controls you asked about. Quick note: I'll reference the security pack we can share after the call.
[01:05] Sara Patel: To kick off, our immediate must-haves: SOC2 or equivalent, customer-managed keys ideally, SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning, and full audit logs retention for 7 years for some products. Sounds like a lot, but that's our baseline.
[01:25] Avery Chen: Totally reasonable. Can you say which parts of your workflows will involve sensitive data — PII, PHI, IP?
[01:35] Ethan Morales: Mostly PII and internal IP. A small subset of PHI in one product line; that's why we have both residency and retention constraints. We also need role-based access controls mapped to our internal groups.
[01:46] Marcus Lee: Understood. On KMS we support several patterns: Redwood-hosted KMS, bring-your-own-KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS), and HSM-backed options for Private deployments. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer keys — but for full on-prem HSM you’d be looking at Private.
[02:20] Priya Kaur: When you say "Hosted with customer keys" — does that mean keys never leave our KMS? We need to ensure crypto material isn't exported.
[02:30] Marcus Lee: Correct — with BYOK we keep the key material in your KMS. Redwood only receives encrypted model payloads and uses the public wrapping. For Dedicated there's a tighter trust boundary; for Private the control plane can be customer-managed.
[03:05] Sara Patel: SOC2 — do you have a current report? We need at least Type II, or a roadmap and compensating controls if it's in progress.
[03:15] Avery Chen: We can share our latest SOC2 Type II report and ISO docs. I'll attach them after the call. For customers needing faster attestation, we can provide evidence packages and references to our third-party audits.
[04:00] Ethan Morales: About audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs, immutable retention for at least 5 years and the ability to stream logs to our SIEM. Can Redwood push logs into our S3 and also provide a webhook / Splunk connector?
[04:20] Marcus Lee: Yes — we have log export hooks. For Hosted and Dedicated you can have logs streamed to a customer-owned S3 or to our observability integration. For Private, you keep logs entirely in your network. Tamper-evidence is provided via signed event chains in Dedicated/Private, though the Hosted model uses append-only stores with integrity checks.
[05:10] Priya Kaur: Another item: SSO. We use Okta and expect SAML + SCIM. Our provisioning teams want group sync and SCIM push. How mature is the integration?
[05:25] Avery Chen: We support SAML 2.0 for authentication and SCIM for provisioning. Most customers use Okta; we can map groups to RBAC roles in Redwood Console. Marcus can follow up with the exact claim mapping and sample SAML metadata.
[06:00] Marcus Lee: Quick clarification — RBAC in Redwood allows role scoping at org/project/model level. We can enforce separation of duties and map to your LDAP/IdP groups. We also support API token rotation and limited-scope tokens for platform automation.
[06:42] Sara Patel: Data residency — we operate in EU and US and some APAC; our policy says certain data must stay in EU. If we use Hosted, can we ensure requests and logs are routed to EU regions only?
[06:55] Marcus Lee: Yes — routing policies can pin requests by region and we support region-specific model variants. For strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated in-region or Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted can be configured for EU-only but there are caveats for backups and third-party services — we'll document those.
[07:40] Ethan Morales: Encryption at rest — are embeddings and prompts encrypted at rest by default? And what about ephemeral caches?
[07:50] Marcus Lee: All customer data at rest is encrypted. Embeddings and prompts stored for caching are encrypted; ephemeral KV cache is in memory and swapped to encrypted disk if necessary. With BYOK we wrap encryption keys with your KMS.
[08:25] Priya Kaur: What about log retention and deletion for legal hold? We may need to delete or freeze records on request.
[08:35] Avery Chen: We support configurable retention policies per workspace and can perform data purges on request with certificate of deletion for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, you control deletion in your environment. Legal-hold workflows are supported via our compliance API.
[09:10] Sara Patel: Have customers run benchmarks for latency and throughput? We need assurance that Dedicated meets our 50ms token latency SLAs for short chats.
[09:20] Marcus Lee: We regularly benchmark on our runtime. For 50ms at token-level, it depends on model and sequence length; Dedicated with pinned GPUs is the recommended path. We can run a short pilot to measure your actual workload.
[10:00] Priya Kaur: Ok that aligns. On the SOC2 timeline, if we decide to pilot in September, we'd still need SOC2 evidence for procurement. Is your SOC2 package sufficient?
[10:12] Avery Chen: We'll share the full Type II report and a supplemental control matrix mapping to Redwood features. For further assurance we can provide references and an architecture review.
[11:00] Ethan Morales: A small nit — are there any multi-tenant risks on Dedicated? We need strict isolation.
[11:10] Marcus Lee: Dedicated provides tenant isolation at compute level. We use dedicated GPU pools with network isolation and separate storage accounts. We'll include the isolation diagram in the follow-up.
[12:00] Priya Kaur: If we go Private, how much operational overhead is expected from our side? We have a small infra team.
[12:10] Marcus Lee: Private is heavier: you'll manage the control plane or run our private control plane in your VPC; we provide an operator package and support. If infra is limited, Dedicated is often the sweet spot — brings most of the control without full ops burden.
[13:00] Sara Patel: About keys: do you support HSM-backed GRANTs and key rotation without downtime?
[13:10] Marcus Lee: Yes — with AWS CloudHSM / External HSM we can rotate keys via KMS without taking inference down. We'll document rotation cadence and the rotation flow.
[14:00] Avery Chen: I'll share a short flow diagram for KMS integration and rotation.
[14:15] Priya Kaur: Are audit logs tamper-evident in the Hosted environment? You mentioned integrity checks earlier but what does that look like for compliance?
[14:25] Marcus Lee: For Hosted we use append-only storage with signed digests daily. For Dedicated/Private we can apply cryptographic signing to create a verifiable chain. We'll include a short write-up in the pack.
[15:10] Ethan Morales: One more: retention windows for embeddings — some teams want indefinite retention for analytics, others want strict 30-day retention. Can retention be set per project?
[15:22] Marcus Lee: Yes per-workspace and per-route retention policies are supported. You can configure TTLs and set auto-purge. For long-term analytics we recommend exporting to your data lake.
[16:00] Priya Kaur: Good. Let's talk timeline: if you send materials by Monday we'll review and aim to start a Dedicated pilot first week of September.
[16:12] Avery Chen: Sounds good — action items noted.
[16:30] Sara Patel: Any legal procurement items we should expect for Dedicated? SOC2, SLAs, data processing addendum?
[16:40] Avery Chen: Yes DPA, SOC2, and standard enterprise SLA for Dedicated. For Private there's a licensing + support model. We'll send a short procurement checklist.
[17:05] Marcus Lee: I'll prepare the architecture diagram and KMS integration notes. Also propose an initial pilot config: two-node Dedicated pool in eu-west with BYOK and full audit log forwarding.
[18:00] Priya Kaur: That pilot config sounds aligned. We'll confirm budget and stakeholders.
[18:20] Ethan Morales: We'll also share our internal compliance questionnaire — expect some follow-ups on key rotation and incident response.
[18:40] Avery Chen: Perfect. To wrap, recap: Redwood sends SOC2/ISO docs, KMS/rotation diagram, Dedicated pilot plan, and SAML/SCIM claim mapping. Customer will share retention policy and compliance questionnaire and confirm target pilot start.
[19:05] Sara Patel: Thanks everyone, that was super helpful.
[19:12] Priya Kaur: Thanks — talk soon.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: security pack (linked after call), Dedicated pilot architecture (will be attached), procurement checklist (link in follow-up).
